svg.title: The Paddock family
svg.desc: Eight local-first desktop apps. Pacenotes, Debrief and Sighter above; Recce, Dyno and Spotter below; Pitwall, the optional local AI hub, between them; Pitcrew under Dyno. Hand-offs: Pacenotes and Debrief exchange stack traces and log checks, Pacenotes sends Sighter test plans and gets results, Sighter sends Debrief run bundles, Debrief drives Sighter over MCP to reproduce a bug from a video, Pitcrew sends Debrief job logs and Dyno sends it issues (one line up the left margin, beside Recce and Pitwall, not through them), Dyno sends Pitcrew machine health and Spotter installed software, Pitcrew runs CI for all, and Spotter will feed Sighter smoke tests later. Uses of Pitwall (dotted): Pacenotes for answers and embeddings, Debrief as its AI engine once paired (its built-in engine is the fallback), Sighter for vision and as agent planner, Recce for answers, Dyno for diagnosis, Spotter for what's-new summaries. Planned for Pitwall 1.1 (dash-dot, labelled MCP): Pitwall as MCP client and host calls the MCP servers of Pacenotes, Debrief, Sighter, Recce (the family's retrieval engine, so Pitwall builds no index of its own) and Dyno (its MCP server is opt-in). Recce (one search box for the whole PC) is planned and shown with its placeholder icon. Underneath, Paddock provides the kits (UI kit and design system, shared Rust crates, diagram kit, icon set, conformance checks, release practices, lessons) and two layers: the App shell every app uses (startup protection and safe mode, Report a problem, background services and login items, notifications and service health, dialogs, jobs and progress, settings, about and updates, the Storage page, undo, theme) and, on top of it, the Workbench for the IDE-style apps Debrief, Pacenotes and Sighter (docked panes with the layout planner, activity bar, Explorer, command palette, AI pane); Pitcrew, Pitwall, Spotter, Dyno and Recce use the shell with pages.
svg.text: Eight local-first apps for people who keep systems running
One private AI hub, one shared foundation. Each app is good alone and better together.
